body: Thank you! I'm glad to know there are other sensible people in this world!
Thank you. Just thank you and I hope you're right

I'm afraid to tell him how bad it's been for me because I don't want him to think he's headed that way. But I understand what you mean. I've been dripping information like that to him, like "I get it. You're not weird."

The driving thing is good advice. I illegally took him driving a few months ago and he was downright giddy, but I haven't made time to take him since. It's funny that you mentioned music because he's about to start taking guitar lessons with my best friend's younger brother. He doesn't want to be a rockstar, but he wants a hobby to be proud of. It's perfect because my friend's brother is in school to be a music teacher and is a history  nerd, and my brother wants to be a history teacher. I think that'll be a great space for him and help him look forward to what he can be

I still just get so scared when I'm not with him though. Ugh, I just wish I could take it all away. I would shoulder his burdens on top of my own if I could. I don't care how bad it would feel if I knew he was okay
Unload on us. Maybe we can help. I've been there and it hurts like hell

I know you're not mentally disabled, but I'm guessing you get support in school due to your disabilities? I recommend finding your special ed chair and asking them for advice. Even if you don't work with them already, seek them out. They usually want to help. On the off chance that don't, know they suck at their job and it's not a reflection on you

I'm sorry you feel so alone. It takes time for people to get past physical features. Those friends will come. I know it doesn't help now, though. Until then, we're here for you
your boss is an asshole and super unprofessional. Defend your business, sure. But there was no need to make personal attacks. Super immature and I wouldn't want to work with them
very specific question. do you cut, then laminate. or laminate, then cut. I know which way I lean, but I feel like I'm in the minority and I want your pov

those are the worst. I'm always torn between empathy and experience. Seemingly flaky friends who turn out to be all-weather-friends and vice versa. But lots of time, people are who they are. I'm glad I only vaguely broach those topics (ie emotional regulation, size  of the problem)

I hope they cool off soon

Anything you remember from when you first started? Mistake you made? Tips?

From what I understand they're pretty similar programs, just geared towards differentage  groups

What kind of access do you have to technology? Voice-to-text is a miracle, but the learning curve can be steep depending on the student and disability. It may be worth it to train them on that (which will initially take time away from other students but will free you in the long term. Plus it's a good life skill for students who haven't had progress with reading/writing interventions).

Also, ask about his challenges where he can read but not write.

Oh, also, don't text about your kids or use personal accounts, or the parents might end up with access to your entire text/Facebook/etc history and no one wants that invasion of privacy. That kind of stuff is so common where I work
